title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Special Tower Number Field Sieve (STNFS) via GT DLP reduction

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity P in G1 and uniform z in GT on BLS12-381, the Special Tower Number Field Sieve (STNFS) attack in proof.md computes g = e(P, Q0) in GT, recovers a in [0, r) satisfying g^a = z in F_{p^12}^* using the degree-6 tower h(Y) = Y^6 - Y^2 + 1 with f_y(X) = X^12 - 2*y*X^10 + 2*y^3*X^6 + y^5*X^2 + y^2 - 1 and g_y(X) = X^2 - u*y at parameters A = 686 and B = 2^65.316, and returns Q = [a]Q0 in G2 satisfying e(P, Q) = z. Under the standard STNFS smoothness, Poisson-Normal relation-yield, filtering, and Block-Wiedemann heuristics disclosed in proof.md, the attack succeeds with probability at least 0.40 (specifically >= 0.90, with relation-collection survival probability P(RF >= SP) > 0.9999 > 0.40) using at most 2^115.560000 total target-group-operation equivalents (normalized by C = 20,000 scalar AArch64 instructions per reference dense F_{p^12} multiplication; corresponding to 2^126.15 raw STNFS model operations and 2^129.847353 scalar AArch64 instructions). Peak memory is at most 2^68.000000 bytes; preprocessing (charging all challenge-independent polynomial selection, factor base, sieving, and linear algebra stages in full without amortization) is at most 2^115.560000 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes (2^0 bytes) and is included in memory.

experiments.purpose: Verify the BLS12-381 STNFS polynomial identities over O_h = Z[y]/(y^6 - y^2 + 1), compute 1/zeta_{K_h}(2) and the exact TNFS Murphy alpha values alpha(f_y, h, B0) and alpha(g_y, h, B0) via prime-ideal root counting and recursive bad-ideal lifting, execute the Monte-Carlo simulation of Murphy's E-function (Algorithm 6.1) at A = 686 and B = 2^65.316 to evaluate the Poisson-Normal survival probability P(RF >= SP), and audit the scalar AArch64 instruction ledger normalized by C = 20,000.
